lotl.label: What's Going On With the Leafs
lotl.body: The quiet of September has a way of telling the truth - this club is not tinkering for the sake of it, it is chiseling away at the final roster picture. Steven Lorentz cleared waivers, a small move on the surface but a revealing one, because it trims the fat and shows Toronto is serious about sorting out its bottom six before camp hardens into decisions. The Leafs enter the deep offseason with their season finished and their attention fixed on the next layer of work. The noise now is about fit, not fireworks: a brief Arizona bonding trip before opening night, and a whiff of intrigue around Kirill Marchenko that hints at ambition without forcing a rush. What comes next is camp, then the first real test of whether this roster has enough bite down the middle and enough legs on the back end.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Jays
lotl.body: The Jays are headed into the winter with a little more clarity - and a little more edge. Vladimir Guerrero Jr. apologized Friday for his contract comments, a public reset that matters because the club's biggest star can't spend September auditioning for a grievance committee. José Soriano's final start of the year also gives the front office one more look at a pitcher who flashed enough to keep in the conversation, though the 5.30 ERA in 10 Jays starts says the search for rotation help is far from over. With Shane Bieber's injury concerns nudging the club toward outside pitching, Toronto has to balance faith in its internal arms against the cold truth of the market. The season is done. The work starts now. What to watch next: how aggressively this club attacks pitching depth before camp opens.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Raptors
lotl.body: The noise around Toronto finally has a pulse again - and it's coming from the biggest name on the board. Kawhi Leonard's two-year, $115 million extension gave the Raptors a headline worthy of the old days, but this isn't nostalgia for nostalgia's sake. It's a bet on a new core, one that has to prove it can live up to the money and the moment. Toronto's season is over, the ledger is closed, and the work now is roster fit, health and timing - especially with Immanuel Quickley positioned as the swing piece in a group that needs his pace and shot-making. Next comes training camp, where the real question is whether this expensive new shape can actually hold together.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Commanders
lotl.body: A franchise lives on hope, but hope gets awfully expensive when the quarterback's elbow becomes the headline. Jayden Daniels is week-to-week and the Commanders have kept surgery and injured reserve off the table - a practical choice, and a revealing one, because it says the organization still believes the season can be steered back on course. Washington enters the offseason without a clean answer in the secondary, with the roster reconstruction now circling the same two questions every team eventually faces: who protects the back end, and who steadies the offense when the passer is absent? Daniels is the story because he has to be; so are the voices saying Diggs and Williams are finding room against man and zone. What to watch next: whether the front office turns that uncertainty into help before camp hardens the depth chart.

two_up.dek: Shane Bieber's back issue is another reminder that Toronto cannot bank on high-upside arms that might not stay available. With the offseason already arriving, the Blue Jays need durability more than name value if they want to stabilize the rotation for 2027.

two_up.headline: What it means for Kawhi Leonard to retire a Raptor
two_up.dek: A Leonard retirement in Toronto would lock in the city's only title run with the franchise and deepen his place in Raptors history. It would also sharpen the debate over how much weight one championship, one Finals MVP, and one season in Toronto should carry in his legacy.

article.title: Saturday's Skate
paragraphs: The Leafs are heading to Arizona for a final camp bonding trip at Auston Matthews' home, with the Kirill Marchenko chatter still hanging around the roster picture. For the Blue Jays, the focus is on sorting out Jose Soriano after his final start, while Shane Bieber's injury concerns are pushing the club to keep looking for pitching help.

The Raptors are deep in the offseason, with new talk framed less by Kawhi Leonard and more by the need to move forward. In Washington, the Commanders are mapping out a fix for the secondary while Jayden Daniels' return is still tied to his elbow, and that leaves Sunday's home opener against the Seahawks with Marcus Mariota in line to start.
